posts.checked: Says Voltaire said, “To learn who rules over you, simply find out who you are not allowed to criticize.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and most replies agree that the quote comes from neo-Nazi Kevin Alfred Strom, not Voltaire.
posts.disagree: One note says the quote's meaning matters more than its source. Many replies ask whether Massie quoted a neo-Nazi on purpose.

posts.checked: A Pfizer executive has admitted the company did not test whether its Covid-19 vaccine stopped transmission of the virus before its launch.
posts.agree: All three agree that Pfizer's trials did not test whether the vaccine stopped transmission.
posts.disagree: The fact-checkers say this was always public and that the vaccine still reduced infection and onward spread. Most notes and replies take it as proof that vaccine passports and pressure to vaccinate rested on a lie.

posts.checked: Illinois “received $5.1 billion at an elementary school there that used it for equity and diversity.”
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. Notes and many replies agree that CRT is an academic theory, not an elementary school curriculum, and that diversity programmes are not CRT.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker addresses the $5.1 billion, which went to some 850 school districts, while the notes argue over what CRT means. Replies mock Greene and call her a liar.

posts.checked: 53% of Americans made aware of the Hunter Biden laptop story would have changed their vote in 2020.
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. Notes and many replies agree that the $3.4 million reimbursed Twitter for legally required responses to subpoenas; the fact-checker addresses only the poll.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates the poll figure false because it covers a small, Republican-leaning subset, while most notes argue only about the FBI payment and defend reading it as payment for censorship. Most replies call Stefanik a liar.

posts.checked: That photo of "apparently an aluxe" was taken "3 days ago," on February 22, 2023, at the supervision of the Maya Train's works.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and several replies agree that the photo has circulated since at least 2021 and was not taken at the Maya Train works.
posts.disagree: The other note says a note would spoil the joke. Most replies mock López Obrador for spreading superstition.

posts.checked: Two photos of Statue Of Liberty, taken in 1898 and 2017, disprove sea level rise
posts.agree: The fact-checkers, one note and a few replies agree that sea levels have risen, though too little to see in two photos given the tides.
posts.disagree: The other note calls the post opinion that mocks exaggerated predictions. Most replies agree with the post that climate warnings have failed.

posts.checked: Photos show that Pennsylvania Sen. John Fetterman has a body double
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and a few replies agree that the photos show the same man, with the differences down to the camera.
posts.disagree: One note says the photo on the right is objectively a different person, and most replies agree with the post. Another note says the post is a joke.

posts.checked: A Minnesota lawmaker introduced a bill that would make it “illegal to discriminate against child rapists.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker and half of the notes agree that the bill removes a line because paedophilia is not a sexual orientation, and that it weakens no law protecting children.
posts.disagree: The other half of the notes say that removing the line does what the post says. Every sampled reply that takes a side accepts the post, and many see a wider push to normalise paedophilia.

posts.checked: This video shows a woman taking real golden pearls out of an oyster shell.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and many replies agree that the pearls were planted and the video is staged.
posts.disagree: Other notes say the post makes no claim that needs a note. Some replies take the pearls as real, and others focus on the harm to the clam.

posts.checked: “(Donald) Trump ran up more debt than any other president in American history.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that Obama added more debt in total, while Trump added the most per year.
posts.disagree: One note says the post is accurate because Trump added the most in a single term. Most replies call Jeffries a liar and blame the pandemic or Congress for the debt.

posts.checked: Photo shows former President Donald Trump “in the hood.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and a few replies agree that the image was generated by AI.
posts.disagree: One note says the post makes no factual claim. Most replies take up the post's question and say Obama looks down on Black neighbourhoods.

posts.checked: These are images of a market where the Islamic State is trading sex slaves.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and most replies agree that the video is a staged scene filmed in Erbil, not a real market. Several add that ISIS did sell Yazidi women as slaves.
posts.disagree: One note says there is not yet evidence that the video is staged. Some replies accuse the poster of spreading hatred against Kurds and Muslims.

posts.checked: This study shows that Pfizer's mRNA vaccine causes cancer.
posts.agree: The fact-checkers and most notes agree that the study does not show the vaccine causes cancer; its own authors say evidence of causality is lacking.
posts.disagree: One note defends the post. Most replies accept it, sharing personal fears or saying vaccine makers skipped safety tests on purpose.

posts.checked: Farmers pump CO2 into greenhouses as plants love it so much. Higher atmospheric CO2 levels would also benefit reforestation by enhancing plant growth and creating more resilient microclimates.
posts.agree: All three agree that greenhouse growers add CO2 to boost plant growth.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates the wider claim partly false, and one note and some replies warn of harms such as ocean acidification. The other note and many replies agree with the post that more CO2 is good for the planet.

posts.checked: French news exaggerated temperatures in Corsica
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that a temperature of about 42°C was recorded in Corsica, at least in one spot.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker says the 32°C footage was filmed the day before, while two notes defend the post, saying 42°C was a local maximum or a surface reading. Most replies go further than the notes, seeing a coordinated campaign to spread fear about the climate.

posts.checked: “The government just stated under oath that they are in possession of UFOs and nonhuman alien bodies.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and one reply agree that a former intelligence officer made the claim, not the government, and that the Pentagon denies it.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the post is fair or that the Pentagon is not to be believed. Most replies that take a side accept the post at face value.

posts.checked: "Illinois is now letting illegal aliens become police officers."
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and one reply agree that the law applies only to non-citizens legally authorised to work in the US.
posts.disagree: One note says the post contains no error. Most replies ignore the law and attack DeSantis's campaign, while a few back him.

posts.checked: "In California, the U.S., they steal and nobody can do anything after the law that decriminalizes the practice of tent robberies amounting to less than $400, and that also prevents commercial employees from coping with whoever wants to steal them."
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and two replies agree that shoplifting under $950 is still a crime in California, punishable by jail and fines.
posts.disagree: One note says only police may intervene, so staff can do nothing. Most replies accept the post and blame Democratic policies.

posts.checked: A video showed President Joe Biden falling asleep during an event with the Maui, Hawaii, wildfire survivors and families.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the full footage shows Biden bowing his head and nodding, not sleeping.
posts.disagree: One note calls the post an opinion. Other replies take the clip as proof that Biden is too old to serve.

posts.checked: "Any time you have an email vote, there's gonna be massive traps in your election."
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and two notes agree that Trump made false claims in the interview.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates Trump's claims about voting by mail false, while most notes say an interview should not be noted. Replies celebrate the interview's audience and say it shows truths the media filter out.

posts.checked: Anyone coming to Ireland can vote in Irish elections
posts.agree: All three agree that non-Irish residents, including asylum seekers, can vote in Irish local elections.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker and one note call the post misleading because only local elections are open to them, and many replies correct it the same way. Two notes say this makes the post accurate, and some replies use it to criticise Ireland's asylum system.

posts.checked: The video shows Americans celebrating after the release of Trump’s mugshot photo.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and most replies agree that the clip is an edited video of football fans, not Americans celebrating.
posts.disagree: The only note says it is a familiar meme that needs no note. A few replies take it at face value and celebrate Trump's arrest.

posts.checked: Video shows everyday scenes of messy NYC Union Square streets
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and a few replies agree that the video shows the aftermath of a chaotic influencer giveaway, not everyday life.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the event was real and recent, so needs no note. Most replies take the scene as typical of New York under Biden and the Democrats.

posts.checked: Video showed a woman barging into a classroom and tearing up a pride flag.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that the video is scripted, made by a crew with recurring actors.
posts.disagree: Almost all replies take the video as real and praise the mother; only two say it is staged.

posts.checked: This video shows the destruction of F35 aircraft in aerial combat with the Cuban military.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the footage comes from the video game Arma 3 and shows an A-10, not an F-35.
posts.disagree: One note calls the post an obvious joke, and many replies treat it as a running gag. A couple play along as if it were real.

posts.checked: Julian Assange claimed that the objective of the Ukraine-Russia conflict was to channel funds from the U.S. and Europe.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and a few replies agree that the clip is from 2011 and about Afghanistan, not Ukraine.
posts.disagree: Some replies say it applies to Ukraine anyway, and most use the clip to argue that the war serves money and the arms industry.

posts.checked: This video relates to the terrorist attack in Brussels on 16 October.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and one note agree that the footage comes from a staged music video, not a celebration of the attack.
posts.disagree: The other note says the video still glorifies a child with a gun. Replies take it as real and blame politicians, some calling for deportations.

posts.checked: This video shows Greta Thunberg advocating sustainable and eco-friendly warfare.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that the clip is not genuine: it is a deepfake made as satire.
posts.disagree: Some notes say the satire label means no note is needed, while others say the label is easy to miss. Many replies treat the clip as real and mock Thunberg.

posts.checked: Iran is surrounded by U.S. military bases.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the early notes agree that the map shows US bases that do not exist, such as in Afghanistan and Pakistan. Some notes and replies agree that, despite these errors, the US does keep many bases near Iran.
posts.disagree: Most notes call the post a joke that needs no correction, while the fact-checker treats the map as a factual claim and rates it mostly false. Replies split over Musk's point: some blame US bases for the tension, others blame Iran's government and accuse Musk of echoing its line.

posts.checked: In this video Daniel Stingo's calling to vote against and make a new social blow and constitutional process.
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and one note agree that the video dates from July 2023 and is taken out of context.
posts.disagree: The other note says Stingo still holds those views. Replies take the clip at face value, and many say it pushes them to vote in favour.

posts.checked: This video shows looting at a Nike store on the 2023 Black Friday.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and one reply agree that the video shows looting during the 2020 George Floyd protests, not Black Friday.
posts.disagree: The other note says Woods was being sarcastic. Most replies play along with the joke or blame Democratic cities.

posts.checked: The posts shows a Palestinian boy, Mohammed Nazzal, faking his injuries.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, the misleading notes and many replies agree that the boy in the video is a different released prisoner, not Nazzal.
posts.disagree: Other notes say Nazzal used his arms normally on release and that the BBC's reporting cannot be trusted. Replies are split: some correct the post, others repeat that Palestinians stage injuries.

posts.checked: “We’ve created close to 800,000 manufacturing jobs since I’ve taken office.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that Biden's figure of close to 800,000 jobs is correct. Notes and many replies agree that most of those jobs came back after the pandemic rather than being new.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates the claim mostly true and calls the job growth the strongest in decades, while the notes call it misleading because most jobs were recovered. Replies go further and call Biden a liar.

posts.checked: A former italian health minister is being investigated for hiding COVID vaccine data
posts.agree: The fact-checker and most notes agree that Speranza was investigated over the slow early pandemic response, not over vaccines, and was cleared.
posts.disagree: One note says the story is real. Replies accept the post and see it as evidence that officials everywhere hid vaccine deaths.

posts.checked: I carried out the parliamentary intervention - urgent, urgent, in a state of higher necessity, with a professional tool put out the fire.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and one note agree that there was no fire hazard: Braun put out the Hanukkah candles in an antisemitic act.
posts.disagree: The other note says no one was hurt. Replies split between praising Braun for defending Poland against Jewish influence and calling for him to be prosecuted.

posts.checked: “New proposed bill in Maine says the state can take custody of a kid if the parents oppose” gender-affirming care
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and one note agree that the bill does not let the state take children from their parents.
posts.disagree: Most notes read the bill's wording as allowing a court to take custody when a child is denied gender-affirming care, close to the post's claim, which the fact-checker rates false. Replies accept the post and see the bill as the state taking children from parents.

posts.checked: If you can hold your breath from A to B as shown in this video, it means your lungs are healthy.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that the test proves nothing about lung health.
posts.disagree: Replies treat the video as a game rather than a health test, joking about smokers and vapers.

posts.checked: Putin has declared the purchase of Alaska to be illegal
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and some replies agree that the decree does not mention Alaska.
posts.disagree: Some notes and replies read the decree as a sign that Russia wants to reclaim lost territory, and one note says several sources confirm the post. Most replies treat the claim as real and answer with defiance towards Russia.

posts.checked: Winston Churchill said that "success isn't final, failure isn't fatal: what counts is the value of continuing."
posts.agree: The fact-checkers and a minority of notes agree that there is no evidence Churchill said the quote. Few replies discuss the quote at all.
posts.disagree: Most notes say the quote's source does not matter or that many sources credit Churchill, while the fact-checkers rate the attribution false. Replies discuss DeSantis's exit and his endorsement of Trump instead.

posts.checked: "Diary by Guillermo Teillier would reveal that during the years 1973 to 1978, he himself commands to execute and disappear more than a hundred comrades"
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and many replies agree that the diary does not exist and the claim is invented.
posts.disagree: The other note points to a different, unrelated allegation against Teillier. Some replies accept the post, saying communists have always killed their own.

posts.checked: Ilhan Omar said “we are an organized society, brothers and sisters, people of the same blood, people who know they are Somalians first, Muslims second,” and that “the U.S. government will only do what Somalians in the U.S. tell them to do. They will do what we want and nothing else.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and half of the notes agree that the speech was mistranslated and that Omar was speaking about her Somali constituents.
posts.disagree: The other notes say the translation is accurate or that its critics offer no evidence. Replies accept the translation and call for Omar to be expelled.

posts.checked: Is this possible?
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and most replies agree that the experiment is fake and the coin hangs from a string.
posts.disagree: The other note says the post only asks a question. A couple of replies take the trick as a real magnetic effect.

posts.checked: The Emergency National Security Supplemental Appropriations Act “accepts 5,000 illegal immigrants a day.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, some notes and several replies agree that the 5,000 figure counts encounters at the border and triggers a closure, rather than being a daily quota of admissions.
posts.disagree: Other notes say the post is correct because asylum claims must still be processed above that figure. Most replies call Scalise a liar for opposing a bill he had not read, while a minority back blocking it.

posts.checked: Since Russia invaded Ukraine, “not a single Western journalist has bothered to interview Putin.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker and a handful of notes agree that Western journalists did try to interview Putin and were turned down by the Kremlin. Some replies share their doubts about Carlson, calling Putin a criminal and the interview unchallenging.
posts.disagree: Most notes say the post is opinion and needs no note, while the fact-checker treats it as a checkable claim and rates it false. Most replies side with Carlson that Western media ignore Russia's side, which the fact-checker and some notes reject.

posts.checked: Boris Johnson spiked peace negotiations after Russia withdrew from Kyiv as a goodwill gesture
posts.agree: Most notes and most replies agree that the interview is legitimate journalism that needs no correction. The fact-checker and a minority of notes agree that Putin made false claims about history and the war, and that Carlson did not challenge them.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates Putin's claims false, while most notes say an interview is opinion and should not be fact-checked. Replies praise the interview for revealing what the media kept hidden, the opposite of the fact-checker's reading.

posts.checked: “The Ukraine supplemental includes a hidden impeachment clause against President Trump”
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and most misleading notes agree that the bill says nothing about impeachment and does not target Trump.
posts.disagree: Several notes call Vance's warning an opinion that cannot be checked, while the fact-checker treats it as a factual claim and rates it false. Replies accept the post's premise and see the bill as a plan by Democrats and the establishment to prolong the war and trap Trump.

posts.checked: Spere's outer wall screen in Las Vegas shows "Blue Image."
posts.agree: The fact-checker, several notes and some replies agree that the image was edited and that the Sphere never showed a blue screen.
posts.disagree: Several notes say the post is an obvious joke that needs no correction, while the fact-checker treats the image as a claim and rates it false. Most replies treat it as a joke about Windows.

posts.checked: Billionaires “rigged” the California Senate primary election through “dishonest means.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and most replies agree that outside spending is legal and that the election was not rigged.
posts.disagree: Two notes say Porter's claim is an opinion about money in politics that needs no note. Replies add that her talk of rigging echoes Trump.

posts.checked: A video shows Pallywood production in Gaza.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and several replies agree that the footage comes from a music video shoot by the Palestinian telecom firm Jawwal.
posts.disagree: One note defends the label 'Pallywood' and the post. Many replies accept the post's claim that Palestinians stage their suffering.

posts.checked: The photo depicting the protesters was generated by artificial intelligence.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and a few replies agree that the photo was generated by AI.
posts.disagree: The other note says the image only illustrates the author's opinion. Most replies reject the call for solidarity, calling farmers privileged or their protests pro-Russian.

posts.checked: The viral photo dates back to May 1, 2022, depicting a May Day demonstration in Cuba.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the photo shows an earlier May Day march, not last week's events.
posts.disagree: One note says the date is not settled. Many replies go beyond the date and call Verhofstadt a liar, and some dispute that ISIS carried out the Moscow attack.

posts.checked: Juan Pablo Luna, a former member of the board of Viva Democracy, forms part of the ciper Chile team.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and one reply agree that Luna only wrote opinion columns for CIPER and is not part of its team.
posts.disagree: One note says notes should not be used for personal defence. A few replies back the senator, while one defends CIPER's reporting on him.

posts.checked: Here's NATO headquarters... That's surprising, isn't it?
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and some replies agree that the image was altered or framed to make the building look like the SS emblem.
posts.disagree: One note invites readers to judge for themselves on Google Earth. Most replies accept the resemblance, and some take it as a sign that Nazism lives on in NATO.

posts.checked: Video shows “child groomer” at city council meeting reacting to “getting exposed”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and many replies agree that the man is a comedian performing a parody.
posts.disagree: The other note says satire needs no note. A few replies take the video as real.

posts.checked: BJP leader Dinesh Lal Yadav’s video is Deepfaq, who is responsible for population growth for berozgari.
posts.agree: All three agree that the video is genuine: a journalist recorded the interview, so the post's deepfake claim is false.
posts.disagree: There is little disagreement. Replies go further than the fact-checker and the notes, accusing Malviya of spreading fake news and threatening critics.

posts.checked: Rahul Gandhi promised ₹1 lakh to unemployed youth
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and one reply agree that Gandhi was describing paid apprenticeships for graduates, and that the clip was cut.
posts.disagree: Other notes say the post simply quotes him. Most replies take the clip at face value and say handouts would make young people lazy.

posts.checked: During the 2024 election, Rahul Gandhi stopped talking about Ambani and Adani.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the misleading notes agree that Rahul Gandhi kept criticising Ambani and Adani during the campaign.
posts.disagree: The other notes say Modi only asked a question. Replies turn the charge back on Modi, saying he is the one close to Adani and should investigate if he suspects black money.

posts.checked: Congress leaders, Rahul Gandhi, promised to give a monthly Rs. one lakh to every poor woman in the country.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and all the notes agree that the Congress manifesto promises Rs 1 lakh a year, not a month.
posts.disagree: Two notes say Gandhi can be heard saying 'per month' in the video, while another says the video was edited. Replies split between mocking the promise as unaffordable and correcting the figure.

posts.checked: Video shows Joe Biden endorsing Trump for 2024 polls
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three; the only note calls the post satire.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker says the clip was cut from a 2020 speech. Replies mostly play along with the endorsement or mock Biden as confused, and only one points out that the clip is old.

posts.checked: Photo behind Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi in a viral pic is Jesus Christ
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and some replies agree that the image is Roerich's Banner of Peace painting, not a picture of Jesus.
posts.disagree: Three notes say the painting is still a Christian image, since it shows the Madonna. Most replies set the facts aside and defend the right to display other religions' images, or attack the poster.

posts.checked: What a wonder! the scene of a dead child in Gaza watching a message on his cell phone.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and some replies agree that the photo comes from a costume event, not from Gaza.
posts.disagree: The only note calls the post a joke that needs no note. Most replies take it as proof that Palestinian casualties are staged, or joke about martyrs.

posts.checked: Manmohan Singh did not click picture with India team after 20087 World Cup win
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and a few replies agree that the 2007 team was photographed with Prime Minister Manmohan Singh before meeting Sonia Gandhi.
posts.disagree: One note says the post never claimed the team skipped the prime minister, only that Sonia Gandhi had no official role. Many replies accuse the poster of spreading half-truths.

posts.checked: Rahul Gandhi falsely attributed a quote by Mahatma Gandhi to Jesus Christ
posts.agree: The fact-checkers, most notes and many replies agree that the quote comes from Jesus's Sermon on the Mount in the Bible, as Rahul Gandhi said.
posts.disagree: One note says the Gospel is not proof that Jesus said it. Some replies set the quote aside and accuse Gandhi of insulting Hindus.

posts.checked: Social media users have posted an image of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and his wife, Olena Zelenska, posing in front of a table covered in stacks of cash.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and a few replies agree that the image was doctored from a photo of Floyd Mayweather.
posts.disagree: Most replies accept the post's message that Zelensky is corrupt, and many repeat a separate claim, also false according to one note, that his wife bought a Bugatti with US money.

posts.checked: Project 25 in the U.S. will make period passports compulsory
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that Project 2025 contains no 'period passport' proposal.
posts.disagree: One note says the plan does restrict reproductive rights, so the post needs no note. Some replies use the post to argue against Project 2025 and Trump.

posts.checked: Reform UK party candidate Mark Matlock, who contested the U.K. general election from Clapham and Brixton Hill, is not a real person.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, the misleading notes and some replies agree that Matlock is a real person, though his campaign photo was edited.
posts.disagree: One note disputes the evidence, calling Private Eye satire, and another says no record of him exists. Many replies take the post's claim seriously and ask for an investigation.

posts.checked: Barack Obama referred to Michelle Obama as Michael
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and one note agree that 'Michael' in the 2011 clip referred to Admiral Mike Mullen.
posts.disagree: The other note calls the post satire. Most replies take it up and repeat the claim that Michelle Obama is secretly a man.

posts.checked: The video shows LBC Radio anchor James O'Brien talking about 'taking a shot at Trump.'
posts.agree: The fact-checker and most notes agree that the audio is fake and that the original broadcast was about Biden's health.
posts.disagree: One note says there is no evidence of a fake. Almost all replies take the clip as real and accuse Ofcom of double standards.

posts.checked: social media user claiming to show a man vandalising a statue in France
posts.agree: The fact-checker and every note agree that the photo is from Algeria in 2017, not France. One reply acknowledges this.
posts.disagree: Replies accept the post's message about Muslim immigration to Europe; one says the location does not change the point.

posts.checked: Fox News broadcast a ticker that reads, "Kamala could be the oldest elected female president."
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and one note agree that the screenshot was altered from a 2018 broadcast.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the post is satire that needs no note. Most replies take the chyron as real and mock Fox, pointing out that Harris would also be the youngest female president.

posts.checked: Former President Jimmy Carter “passed away Tuesday, July 23, at 01:34 am at his home in Plains, Georgia at the age of 99.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and some replies agree that Carter was alive and that the letter was fake.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the post was an obvious joke or a test of who reads beyond the headline, as the poster says in replies. Some replies took the death as real.

posts.checked: Bulgaria had adopted a law prohibiting the use of burkas in public places, institutions, schools and government office. Non-compliance with the law are excluded from social assistance and a fine of €850 will be imposed. Do you support this MOBILE?
posts.agree: The fact-checker and two notes agree that Bulgaria passed its burka ban in 2016, not recently.
posts.disagree: One note says the post never claims the law is new. Replies do not discuss the date; they welcome the ban and call for deportations.

posts.checked: Video shows dog being rescued after Wayanad landslide.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, both notes and a few replies agree that the video is from 2021, not the recent Wayanad landslide.
posts.disagree: Most replies take the video at face value and praise the rescuers.

posts.checked: post on X (formerly Twitter) claiming that goosegrass can reverse kidney failure in three months
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checkers find no evidence that the plant reverses kidney failure, and two notes warn that eating it can be harmful.
posts.disagree: One note says the plant has proven medical benefits. Replies mostly treat it as a common weed, and some accept the post's message that nature heals.

posts.checked: “When Tim Walz was asked by his country to go to Iraq, you know what he did? He dropped out of the Army and allowed his unit to go without him.”
posts.agree: The fact-checkers, the misleading notes and many replies agree that Walz served for 24 years and retired before his unit was ordered to Iraq.
posts.disagree: Most notes say Vance's post is accurate, adding that Walz knew a deployment was coming and was later demoted, while the fact-checkers rate it mostly false or lacking context. Replies reject the post and turn to Vance's and Trump's own records.

posts.checked: Donald Trump “took away protections against discrimination for LGBTQ patients under the Affordable Care Act.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker and some notes agree that Trump's administration reversed Obama-era health care protections for LGBTQ+ people.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates Harris's claim mostly true, while most misleading notes and most replies say Trump never targeted LGBTQ+ people. Some replies welcome the policies Harris objects to, such as limits on transgender athletes.

posts.checked: Kamala Harris is a border czar, Trump built hundred of miles of the border wall, global warming is not a threat
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and a few notes agree that Trump made false or exaggerated claims during the conversation.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates Trump's claims about Harris, the border wall and climate false, while most notes say a conversation should not be noted at all. Replies do not discuss these claims: they back Trump or complain that the Space would not load.

posts.checked: image on X (formerly Twitter), purportedly of United States President-elect Donald Trump with Jeffrey Epstein
posts.agree: No one defends this particular image: the fact-checker rates it fake, and the note and many replies accept that. The note and several replies add that Trump and Epstein were in fact friends.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates the image fake, while the only note says the friendship it implies is real. Replies split between calling it a defamatory fake and posting genuine photos of the two men together.

posts.checked: Photo from an Aug. 14 campaign event in Michigan shows “JD Vance couldn’t fill a small room.”
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and some replies agree that the photo was taken before the rally began.
posts.disagree: The only note says the event was small whatever the timing, in line with the post, and many replies mock Vance's crowd. Other replies call the post dishonest or say Harris's crowds are paid.

posts.checked: Image shows Belgian woman sexually Assaulted for 5 Days by Muslims in Pakistan
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and several replies agree that the photo shows a Czech model arrested for drug smuggling in 2018, not the woman in the story.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the photo is only illustrative and that the assault story is true. Many replies take the story as true and say women should not travel to Pakistan, while others accuse the poster of spreading fake news.

posts.checked: This is a video of the removal of railway track in India.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and many replies agree that the video is from Karachi, Pakistan, not India.
posts.disagree: One note says the post never claimed the video was from India. Some replies back the call to shoot saboteurs, while others want the poster banned for spreading hatred.

posts.checked: The Netflix series 'IC 814' has changed the names of the kidnappers to 'Hindu'.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, two notes and a few replies agree that Bhola and Shankar were code names the hijackers actually used.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the series does not make clear they were code names. Most replies accept the post's charge that the series hides the hijackers' Muslim identity.

posts.checked: The creators of the show "IC 814"changed the name of the hijackers to Hindu names
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the hijackers really used these Hindu code names.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the series still whitewashes the hijackers by not making the disguise clear. Replies split between correcting the poster and calling for action against the director.

posts.checked: Woman seen with Rahul Gandhi is former Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's daughter Amrit Singh
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the woman is Amulya Gopalakrishnan, not Amrit Singh.
posts.disagree: One note says the post only asks a question. Replies split between those who correct the poster and call it fake news, and those who back him and his claim of links to Soros.

posts.checked: CPI(M) general secretary Sitaram Yechury was a Christian.
posts.agree: The fact-checkers, two notes and many replies agree that Yechury was born Hindu and that a coffin says nothing about religion.
posts.disagree: Two notes say the coffin shows Christian funeral rites. Some replies agree with the post that opposition leaders are secretly Christian, while many condemn it for trolling the dead.

posts.checked: The video shows moments of Israel bombing on Hezbollah bases in Lebanon.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, every note and several replies agree that the clips show earlier Israeli strikes in Gaza, not the strike in Lebanon.
posts.disagree: Most replies take the video as genuine and argue over the strikes themselves, some praising their precision and others condemning the harm to civilians.

posts.checked: A humorous video of an American woman not wearing a hijab
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and several replies agree that the woman is Bangladeshi actress Mishti Subas, heckled for celebrating Sheikh Hasina's birthday.
posts.disagree: The other note questions the sources, and one reply says she was attacked whatever the reason. Other replies use the video to attack Bangladesh.

posts.checked: "Hurricane Milton is targeted geo-engineered storm being used as a weapon."
posts.agree: The fact-checker and one note agree that no one can create or steer a hurricane, and that other storms have taken similar paths.
posts.disagree: The other note only objects to Wikipedia as a source. Most replies accept the post and link the storm to other supposedly planned disasters, while a few call it nonsense.

posts.checked: Obama endorsed the use of conspiracy theories to erode a population's trust in each other and public institutions
posts.agree: The fact-checker and two notes agree that Obama was describing how authoritarian regimes use disinformation, not endorsing it.
posts.disagree: Two notes defend the post, one citing a 2012 law on government information. Most replies accept the post and call Obama evil.

posts.checked: (Image) "NASA has just taken this photo of Jupiter": # False
posts.agree: The fact-checker and two notes agree that the image is not a photo of Jupiter, and one of those notes also calls it a joke.
posts.disagree: The third note says an obvious joke needs no note. Many replies get the joke, pointing to the ducks in the 'lagoon', while a few take it as a real photo.

posts.checked: "This is likely to violently violate the 2+4 Treaty, because it unequivocally stipulates that no NATO troops may be stationed in East Germany," writes a user on X in a post that has been displayed more than 340,000 times and shared more than 1,900 times. In addition, the user quotes the headline of the German Baltic Sea newspaper: "NATO opens new headquarters in Rostock".
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker, one note and many replies agree that the new headquarters, run by the German navy, does not breach the 2+4 Treaty.
posts.disagree: Two notes defend the post's reading of the treaty, and many replies see the headquarters as a Western provocation towards Russia.

posts.checked: Tim Walz said, “We can't have four more years of this" about the Biden-Harris administration
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three; the only note says the post needs no note.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker says Walz was speaking about Trump, not about his own administration. Almost all replies take the clip at face value as Walz turning on Harris.

posts.checked: The nails of Ram Gopal Mishra were pulled in the Bahrain Violence, attacked by the pointed weapon on the head, were wounds near the eyes and were given electric shocks.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that police found no sign of torture and that he died from bleeding after being shot.
posts.disagree: One note says the post relies on the widely reported post-mortem. Replies go further, calling the anchor a hate-monger who stirs up riots.

posts.checked: "Reports from Whitfield County, GA that Dominion machines are flipping votes. This is exactly the kind of fraud we saw in 2020."
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that there was no machine problem in Whitfield County and that Dominion fraud claims have been debunked.
posts.disagree: One note says the post only relays reports. A minority of replies accept the post and see a repeat of 2020.

posts.checked: Michigan has “more registered voters than eligible citizens. This creates a huge risk of election fraud.”
posts.agree: All three agree that Michigan's voter rolls contain many records that should be removed, but not on what that means.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker says the extra registrations are inactive records that cannot vote and pose no fraud risk. Replies and some notes treat them as a sign of fraud or of corrupt officials.

posts.checked: “BREAKING: Lizzo charged the Harris-Walz campaign $2.3 million for a single appearance at a Detroit rally.”
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three; the only note defends the post.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker found no evidence the campaign paid Lizzo, while the only note says the figure is correct. Replies split: some accept the figure and say paid celebrities do not really support Harris, others ask for a source or call it a lie.

posts.checked: A video shows Muslims throwing stones at the Uttarkashi rally.
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and one note agree that police did not identify the stone-throwers as Muslims.
posts.disagree: The other notes say the stone-throwers can be presumed Muslim until police say otherwise. Replies accept the post's premise and call for Muslims to be driven out of Uttarakhand.

posts.checked: Video shows “ballot mule in Northampton County, Pennsylvania, (dropping) off a large amount of ballots.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and a few replies agree that the man is a long-serving postal worker lawfully delivering mail ballots.
posts.disagree: One note says his past job in Rhode Island warrants an investigation. Many replies treat him as suspect, questioning his car and licence plate, and urge others to watch for fraud.

posts.checked: Video shows “voting machines in Kentucky are not allowing voters to select” Donald Trump for president.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and several notes agree that the voter tapped a small checkbox rather than the name field, and that her ballot was cast correctly. A few replies describe the same user error.
posts.disagree: Other notes say a machine should never select a different candidate, whatever the user does. Most replies accept the post's claim that machine errors favour Democrats and call for paper ballots.

posts.checked: A purported screenshot from a CNN broadcast allegedly shows Democratic candidate and current Vice President Kamala Harris leading Republican candidate Donald Trump in Texas.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the screenshot is doctored and that CNN never aired these numbers.
posts.disagree: One note reads the post as commentary that needs no note. Replies mostly urge Republicans to vote and say Texas will not turn blue, while a few repeat that the election is being stolen.

posts.checked: A pre-marked dot on the U.S. election ballot makes the vote void.
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and one note agree that officials found no pre-printed dots and that a stray dot would not void a vote.
posts.disagree: The other note says the photo may still be genuine and voters should ask for a clean ballot. Most replies read the dots as a deliberate attempt to cheat in favour of Democrats.

posts.checked: This video shows Nancy Pelosi speaking after Donald Trump's victory.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and one reply agree that the clip is from 2022, after Roe v. Wade was overturned, not after the 2024 election.
posts.disagree: The other note says the post never claims the clip is about the election. Most replies take it as Pelosi reacting to Trump's win and celebrate.

posts.checked: post on X (formerly Twitter), with an image purportedly of thousands of tractors heading to London
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and most replies agree that the photo shows a 2023 farmers' protest in Germany, not tractors heading to London.
posts.disagree: The other note says the photo is only illustrative. A few replies back the farmers and attack Labour.

posts.checked: Udhayanidhi Stalin said that he was a proud Christian.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and many replies agree that the clip is cut: Stalin also said he was Muslim and Hindu, presenting himself as common to all religions.
posts.disagree: One note defends the post's reading. Some replies accept the post and say Stalin disrespects Hindus, while others call the poster a spreader of fake news.

posts.checked: Arvind Kejriwal said BR Ambedkar wrote the Constitution of India while drunk
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and most replies agree that the clip is cropped: Kejriwal was joking about the Congress party's constitution, not India's.
posts.disagree: One note says a public figure should not say such things at all. A few replies take the clip at face value and call for his arrest.

posts.checked: "Oregon sent 60 fire trucks to California to help with the fires, but they’re being held in Sacramento for emissions testing."
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and several replies agree that the trucks only had routine safety checks and went on to fight the fires.
posts.disagree: One note says safety checks usually include emissions. Many replies accept the post and blame California's regulations and Democratic leaders.

posts.checked: Wife Eligible for Family Pension Even if She Murders Husband, Says Punjab and Haryana Court
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that a court granted the pension in 2021, and most notes add that it was stopped once the wife was convicted.
posts.disagree: One note and the poster say the later reversal does not change the original ruling. Replies take the headline at face value and condemn the courts as unfair to men.

posts.checked: Former USAID Administrator Samantha Power’s net worth “skyrocketed” from $6.7 million to $30 million in three years.
posts.agree: No claim is shared by all three. The fact-checker and most misleading notes agree that Power's financial disclosures show no such rise in her wealth.
posts.disagree: Several notes argue over how share sales affect net worth, or say a question needs no note, while the fact-checker rates the figures false. Replies accept the post's figures and call for Power to be investigated.

posts.checked: post shared on X (formerly Twitter) claiming that former Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) chairs Wafula Chebukati and Samuel Kivuitu died two years after overseeing elections
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and several replies agree that Kivuitu died more than five years after the 2007 election, so the dates do not match.
posts.disagree: The other note says the dates matter less than the two men's shared fate. Many replies see the deaths as a curse or punishment for overturning election results.

posts.checked: Britain’s Foreign Secretary, David Lammy, has personally spent over £521,525 in food and drink expenses in less than a year in office.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and two notes agree that the figure covers the whole Foreign Office, not Lammy alone. One reply says the same.
posts.disagree: Another note says the post contains no factual error. Most replies take the figure as Lammy's own and attack him personally.

posts.checked: (Image) "Arresting warrant against Angel Valencia for non-payment of maintenance": # False
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and one reply agree that the image shows a request filed with a court, not an arrest warrant.
posts.disagree: The other note says Valencia was indeed sued for unpaid support, though an appeal suspended the measures. Some replies take the warrant as real, while others criticise the poster.

posts.checked: "Republicans just voted in the House Judiciary Committee to allow Trump to DEPORT U.S. citizens to a foreign country."
posts.agree: The fact-checker and the notes agree that Republicans voted against an amendment barring the deportation of citizens, which is not the same as authorising it. Many replies also reject the post.
posts.disagree: One note argues that the law matters little to this administration. Replies split between calling Swalwell a liar and taking the vote as proof of what Republicans intend.

posts.checked: Headline said, “Pope Leo XIV was a founding member of the 2020 anarchist Portland Autonomous Zone known as CHAZ.”
posts.agree: The fact-checker, most notes and several replies agree that the headline is fake, and many point out that CHAZ was in Seattle, not Portland.
posts.disagree: One note says the joke misleads no one. Some replies play along, and a few take the headline as real.

posts.checked: A social media user claims to show "[f]irst images of the truck driver at Irkutsk airbase" and included a photo of what's made to look like an ID card from Ukraine.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and most replies agree that the image does not show the Irkutsk attacker: it is comedian Sam Hyde, a running joke.
posts.disagree: One note insists it shows a Ukrainian captured by the FSB, and another says a well-known joke needs no note.

posts.checked: California has lower homicide rates than Alabama, Arkansas and Oklahoma.
posts.agree: The fact-checker and some notes agree that Alabama's homicide rate is far higher than California's.
posts.disagree: The fact-checker rates Newsom's comparison mostly true, while some notes dispute the exact ratio and ranking, or the completeness of California's data. Replies rarely dispute the figures: many attribute Alabama's rate to its Black population, or say California's rate is low because it does not prosecute crime.

posts.checked: video, shared on X (formerly Twitter), supposedly showing a pro-Israel march
posts.agree: The fact-checker, the notes and most replies agree that the video is AI-generated.
posts.disagree: A few replies insist it is real, and several share the post's hope that Iranians will turn against their government.

posts.checked: (Image) "They report fire at TEMU winery in China": # False
posts.agree: The fact-checker and one note agree that the image is AI-generated.
posts.disagree: The other note calls the post a joke, and replies treat it as one, joking about their Temu orders.

posts.checked: A form of weather modification called cloud seeding caused the July 4 flash flooding along the Guadalupe River in Texas.
posts.agree: The fact-checker, one note and one reply agree that cloud seeding could not have caused the floods and that Rainmaker was not operating in the area on July 3 or 4.
posts.disagree: The other note says the post only claimed seeding two days earlier. Most replies accept that cloud seeding caused the floods.
